# h3_vm (Resource)

Manages an h3llo cloud virtual machine.

Changed in place: `cpu`, `memory`, `allow_restart_on_resize`, `ssh_key_ids`/`ssh_key_id` (live), `ssh_access_managed` (a running VM restarts), `eip_id`, `release_eip_on_destroy`, `deletion_protection` (live). An increase of `cpu`/`memory` within the live reserve of a running VM is applied without a restart; other CPU/memory changes restart the VM (see `allow_restart_on_resize`). Any other argument change **replaces the VM, and its root disk with all data is deleted** — keep data on a separate `h3_disk` and consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "h3_vm" "web" {
  project_id = var.project_id
  name       = "web-1"
  cpu        = 2
  memory     = "4Gi"
  image      = "ubuntu:24.04"
  disk_size  = "30Gi"
  # Your h3ssh keys; changed in place without a restart.
  ssh_key_ids = [h3_ssh_key.deploy.id]

  subnet_name = h3_network.app.subnet_name
  white_ip    = true

  # cpu and memory change in place: an increase within the live reserve of the
  # running VM (4x its size at start) is applied without a restart, anything
  # else restarts the VM. false: never restart, such a change fails instead.
  allow_restart_on_resize = true

  # cloud-init user-data: runs once on the first boot; changing it replaces the VM.
  user_data = file("${path.module}/cloud-init.yaml")

  # Refuse deletion through the API until set back to false (changed in place).
  deletion_protection = true

  # ssh_key_ids change in place (live);
  # image, disk_size and subnet_name replace the VM together with its root disk.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cpu` (Number) Number of vCPU. Changed in place. An increase up to the live reserve of the running VM (new VMs start with a reserve of 4x their vCPU) is applied **without a restart**; a decrease, an increase above the reserve, an image without CPU hotplug or a VM that cannot be live-migrated needs a **restart** (allowed by `allow_restart_on_resize`, default true). Platforms without live resize always restart the VM.
- `memory` (String) Memory, Kubernetes quantity (e.g. `4Gi`, `2048Mi`). Changed in place. An increase up to the live reserve of the running VM (new VMs start with a reserve of 4x their memory; live changes in multiples of `2Mi`) is applied **without a restart**; a decrease or any other change needs a **restart** (allowed by `allow_restart_on_resize`, default true). Platforms without live resize always restart the VM.
- `name` (String) VM name (1-63 chars: lowercase letters, digits, `-`). Changing it replaces the VM.

### Optional

- `allow_restart_on_resize` (Boolean) Allow the platform to restart the VM when a `cpu`/`memory` change cannot be applied to the running VM (default: true, as before live resize). With `false` such a change fails with `RESIZE_RESTART_REQUIRED` and nothing is changed, so an apply never restarts the VM; only changes that need no restart succeed (a live increase within the reserve, or any change of a stopped VM, which applies at its next start). `false` requires a platform with live resize (the apply fails before any change otherwise). When the VM is busy (live migration or another change in progress), the provider retries for a few minutes.
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Protect the VM from deletion (default: false). While it is `true`, the API refuses to delete the VM (409 `VM_DELETION_PROTECTED`), so `terraform destroy` and a replacement fail: set it to `false` and apply first. Changed in place, the VM is not restarted.
- `disk_size` (String) Root disk size (e.g. `25Gi`); requires `image`. Defaults to the image minimum. Changing it **replaces the VM** — the root disk cannot be resized through the VM API.
- `eip_id` (String) ID (UUID) of an existing, free Elastic IP of the project to use as the VM public IP. Requires `white_ip = true`. If omitted with `white_ip = true`, a new EIP is allocated and its ID is exported here (on platform versions that report it). Changing it moves the public IP in place (the previous EIP is detached and stays in the project); removing it from the configuration keeps the current EIP. An EIP already attached to or reserved by another resource is rejected (409 `EIP_ALREADY_BOUND`).
- `image` (String) OS image id (e.g. `ubuntu:24.04`). Available ids, their minimums (disk, memory, CPU) and status come from the `h3_vm_images` data source; an image missing from it is rejected (400 unknown/not offered, 409 temporarily unavailable). A custom image of the project is `custom:<id>` (the `image` attribute of `h3_vm_image`); it needs `disk_size` of at least its `size_gi`. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `placement_group_id` (String) ID of an `h3_vm_placement_group` (strategy `spread`: every VM of the group runs on its own host). Set at creation only: changing it **replaces the VM**. Removing it from the configuration keeps the VM in its group. A full group answers 409 `PLACEMENT_GROUP_FULL`.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (UUID). Defaults to the provider `project_id` (`H3_PROJECT_ID`). Changing it replaces the VM.
- `release_eip_on_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the VM's Elastic IP together with the VM (default: false). By default destroying the VM keeps its public IP in the project as a free EIP, and it continues to be billed until released.
- `source_backup_id` (String) Create the VM from this backup. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `source_snapshot_id` (String) Create the VM from this snapshot (UUID). Changing it replaces the VM.
- `ssh_access_managed` (Boolean) The platform keeps `/home/user/.ssh/authorized_keys` in sync with `ssh_key_ids` and `h3_vm_ssh_access` grants through qemu-guest-agent. Defaults to `true` on images with the agent; null where the platform does not offer SSH access management. **Changing it on a running VM restarts the VM.** When it is on, keys added to `authorized_keys` by hand inside the VM are removed; keep your own keys in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys2`.
- `ssh_key_id` (String, Deprecated) ID of one `h3_ssh_key`. **Deprecated:** use `ssh_key_ids`. Conflicts with `ssh_key_ids`. Changed in place (it no longer replaces the VM).
- `ssh_key_ids` (Set of String) IDs of your `h3_ssh_key` keys that may log in as `user`. Changed in place, without a restart, when SSH access is managed by the platform (`ssh_access_managed`); otherwise the keys are written only on the first boot. This is your own grant on the VM (mode `selected`); `[]` revokes it. Without the argument Terraform does not change the keys. The current keys are read from the VM's SSH access once the provider knows which grant is yours (after it created the VM or changed the keys; after an import, the grant made at creation). One key works on platforms without SSH access management; two or more need it. Keys of other project members are granted with `h3_vm_ssh_access`.
- `subnet_name` (String) Subnet to place the VM in: the `subnet_name` of an `h3_network`. The project default subnet when omitted. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `user_data` (String) Your cloud-init user-data (up to 64 KiB): a `#cloud-config` YAML document, a `#!` shell script or a `#cloud-boothook`. It runs once, on the first boot, after the platform configuration (user `user`, SSH keys, console password), which keeps working: your `users`, `runcmd`, `write_files` and other lists are appended to the platform ones. Only for a new Linux VM from an image (not with `source_snapshot_id`/`source_backup_id`). gzip, MIME multipart and `#include` are not accepted. The API never returns user-data, so the provider keeps the configured value in state and does not log it; **changing it replaces the VM** (cloud-init would not run it again). After `terraform import` the value is unknown: add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [user_data] }` to keep the imported VM.
- `user_data_encoding` (String) Encoding of `user_data`: `plain` (default) or `base64` (e.g. `base64encode(file("init.yaml"))`). Requires `user_data`. Changing it replaces the VM.
- `white_ip` (Boolean) Give the VM a public IP (default: false). Without `eip_id` a new Elastic IP is allocated in the project. Changed in place: `true` attaches `eip_id` (or a newly leased EIP), `false` detaches the current EIP, which stays in the project as a free, billed EIP unless `release_eip_on_destroy = true`.

### Read-Only

- `endpoint` (String) Public IP address when `white_ip` is true, empty otherwise
- `id` (String) VM ID
- `internal_ip` (String) Private IP address in the project network
- `status` (String) VM status (`PENDING`, `RUNNING`, ...)
- `subnet_id` (String) ID of the subnet the VM is placed in
- `vpc_id` (String) ID of the VPC the VM is placed in

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by ID
terraform import h3_vm.example <id>
```
